title: Odd and even: partners and equal groups

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here are eight mittens, all mixed up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide each mitten next to its partner. One pair, two pairs, three pairs, four pairs.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Every mitten has a partner, so eight is even.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: That mitten has no partner, so nine is an odd number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the cups by twos. How many cups are there?

do.text: Count the cups by 2s. How many cups are there?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Two, four, six, eight, ten, twelve. There are twelve.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The last cup has no partner. Ten, and one more is eleven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One cup is left over, so eleven is an odd number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: There are fourteen socks. Put them in two equal groups. Which equation shows the fourteen socks?

do.text: There are 14 socks. Put them in two equal groups. Which equation shows the 14 socks?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Split each pair: one sock goes up, and its partner stays. Two, three, four, five, six, seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seven on top, and seven on the bottom. Fourteen equals seven plus seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more sock makes fifteen: seven, seven, and one left over. Fifteen is odd.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: An even number splits into two equal groups.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every one has a partner: even. One left over: odd.

do.text: Every one has a partner: even.
